d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 3. Desert Regions
d.notions: Aridity, diurnal temperature range, relative humidity, sandstorm, Harmattan, Sirocco, Khamsin.
d.focus: Characteristics of the climate of hot deserts, with the example of Aswan (Egypt).
d.competence: Learners are able to protect themselves from extreme heat and dust, and to explain why desert nights are cold.
objectives: Describe the rainfall of hot deserts.
Describe the temperatures of hot deserts and explain the large daily range.
Describe the winds and humidity of hot deserts.
recall: Hot deserts lie between 15° and 30° north and south of the Equator.
They are caused by dry trade winds, cold ocean currents, distance from the sea and rain shadow.
There are sandy (erg), stony (reg) and rocky (hamada) deserts.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: day and night temperatures in Garoua in March.
situation: Oumarou, a truck driver from Garoua, drives across the Sahara to Algeria. During the day, the heat is so strong that he cannot touch the metal of his truck.
But at night, he is so cold that he must cover himself with a thick blanket. Oumarou cannot understand how the same place can be so hot by day and so cold at night.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Oumarou does not understand why the desert is so hot during the day and so cold at night.
What does Oumarou need at night in the desert?
He needs a thick blanket, because the nights are cold.
What advice can you give to a traveller crossing the desert?
He should carry a lot of water, wear light clothes by day, have warm clothes for the night and travel with a guide.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the climate of hot deserts and to compare it with the climate of Garoua.

qa.q: Aswan, in Egypt, receives only about 2 mm of rain per year. How does this compare with Garoua, which receives about 1,000 mm?
qa.a: Aswan receives about 500 times less rain than Garoua. It is one of the driest places on Earth.

qa.q: In the desert, rain may not fall for several years, and then a sudden storm causes floods. What does this tell us about desert rainfall?
qa.a: Desert rainfall is very low and very irregular. When it falls, it often comes as short, violent storms.

sum.title: I. Rainfall and Humidity
sum.intro: Rainfall and humidity in hot deserts have the following characteristics:
items: A. Very Low Rainfall
Hot deserts receive less than 250 mm of rain per year. Aswan in Egypt receives only about 2 mm.
B. Irregular Rainfall
Rain may not fall for years. When it falls, it comes as short, violent storms that can cause floods.
C. Low Humidity and Clear Skies
The air is very dry and there are almost no clouds, so the sun shines strongly nearly every day.

qa.q: Study the graph. What is the mean daily maximum temperature in Aswan in July, and in January?
qa.a: In July, the mean daily maximum is about 42°C. In January, it is about 23°C.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: In July, days reach about 42°C and nights about 28°C. Calculate the daily (diurnal) temperature range.
qa.a: The daily temperature range is 42°C − 28°C = 14°C. In winter, it is also about 13°C.

qa.q: Why does the desert become cold at night, when there are no clouds?
qa.a: Without clouds, the heat stored by the ground during the day escapes quickly into the sky at night, so the air cools down fast.

sum.title: II. Temperatures
sum.intro: The temperatures of hot deserts have the following characteristics:
items: A. Very Hot Days
Summer days are very hot, often above 40°C. In Aswan, the mean daily maximum in July is about 42°C.
aswan_climate.png
B. Cold Nights
Nights are much cooler, because the clear skies let the heat escape. The daily temperature range can be 15°C or more.
C. Cool Winters
Winters are cooler than summers. In Aswan, January days reach about 23°C and nights about 10°C.

qa.q: Name the hot, dusty wind that blows from the Sahara over Garoua in the dry season.
qa.a: It is the Harmattan. Other hot desert winds are the Sirocco, which blows towards Italy, and the Khamsin, which blows over Egypt.

qa.q: Strong winds lift sand and dust into the air. What do we call this, and what are its dangers?
qa.a: This is a sandstorm. It makes it difficult to see and to breathe, and it damages crops, roads and machines.

sum.title: III. Winds
sum.intro: The winds of hot deserts have the following characteristics:
items: A. Hot, Dry Winds
Hot, dry and dusty winds blow from the deserts, such as the Harmattan (West Africa), the Sirocco (North Africa) and the Khamsin (Egypt).
B. Sandstorms
Strong winds lift sand and dust into the air. Sandstorms reduce visibility and damage crops, roads and machines.

evaluation: Give two characteristics of the rainfall of hot deserts.
The rainfall of hot deserts is very low, less than 250 mm, and very irregular.
Why is the daily temperature range large in hot deserts?
It is large because the clear skies let the ground heat strongly during the day and lose its heat quickly at night.
Two hot desert winds are the Harmattan and the Sirocco.
remediation: Hot deserts receive less than ______ mm of rain per year.
Aswan in Egypt receives about ______ mm of rain per year.
Desert nights are cold because there are no ______.
The difference between day and night temperatures is the ______ temperature range.
The dusty wind that blows over Garoua is the ______.
A storm of sand lifted by strong winds is a ______.
